::: {.callout-warning}
## Integrated implementation, unaccepted semantic scope

This page is the sole target authority for SCNSim parameter definitions,
physical Plan binding, operation-time points and spaces, sweep Results,
optimization binding, and parameterized diagrams. The target is
`CONVERGING` with an integrated implementation baseline. This is not Human
acceptance. The centralized [implementation and evidence status](index.qmd#implementation-evidence-status)
limits execution claims. Accepted physical models, numerical algorithms,
Views, quantities, and evidence rules remain unchanged unless this page
explicitly reopens their parameter identity or batching boundary.
:::

## Ownership model {#parameter-ownership-model}

Five owners remain separate:

| Owner | Owns |
|---|---|
| `ParameterDefinitions` | independent names, schemas, and immutable baseline values |
| `CircuitPlan` | the exact definition-and-consumer closure reached through registered physical fields |
| `ParameterSet` or `ParameterSpace` | one selected point or an ordered collection of selected points |
| calculation request | one Plan, one View, one Spec, and the operation to perform |
| Result and receipt | the effective point, request identity, evidence, outcome, and stored artifacts |

There is no mutable global current value, implicit Plan registry, expression
engine, GUI authoring state, or hidden batch service. ASCDLS projects a Plan at
one explicit point; it never chooses a View or executes analysis.

The [shared assembly contract](circuit-plan-assembly.qmd) owns the physical
model consumed here. Resolving a frozen Plan snapshot and `ParameterSet` uses
shared physical-field validation, not a diagram import or render preflight.
Parameter and Calculation use remain available when a diagram cannot be laid
out; no presentation choice writes definitions, Plan state, or requests.

## Independent definitions and immutable refs {#independent-parameter-definitions}

The target public declarations are:

```text
ParameterValue := ScalarPintQuantity | RLGC
ParameterSpec(*, unit: Unit) -> ParameterSpec
RLGCParameterSpec(
    *, conductors: tuple[str, ...], reference_conductor: str,
) -> RLGCParameterSpec
ParameterDefinitions(*, id: str) -> ParameterDefinitions
ParameterDefinitions.parameter(
    *, id: str, baseline: ParameterValue,
    spec: ParameterSpec | RLGCParameterSpec,
) -> ParameterRef
ParameterRef.show() -> HtmlPresentation
ParameterDefinitions.show() -> HtmlPresentation
```

`ScalarPintQuantity` is contract notation for a scalar `pint.Quantity` that
passes the existing dimensional, unit, and finite-value validation. It is not
a new importable wrapper class.

A `ParameterRef` identity key is exactly its definitions-collection ID and
local parameter ID. Exact schema and canonical baseline-definition agreement
are compatibility facts for that key, not extra identity fields that permit
conflicting definitions to coexist. Its identity is not a Python address,
component occurrence, child path, or display label. One collection may
accumulate definitions, but an existing definition cannot be rebound, mutated,
or silently overwritten.

`ParameterSpec` validates one scalar Quantity's unit and dimensionality. It
does not own optimization bounds, a target, a Gate, or mutability.
`RLGCParameterSpec` validates one complete fixed-basis RLGC value: the declared
non-reference conductor order and reference conductor determine the matrix
shape; R/L/G/C retain their existing per-length dimensions. It does not own
matrices, extraction provenance, `n_sections`, or optimizer bounds.

`show()` on a ref or definitions collection displays that independent
definition only. It cannot claim a global list of consuming Plans or private
children.

For the Spec and Result owners enumerated below, retained Quantity, array, and
mapping values are detached from the caller at construction or verified decode.
Their public getters return a safe immutable view or a detached small value:
normal calls such as in-place Pint conversion or re-enabling an ndarray write
flag cannot mutate those Specs or Results. `ParameterRef`, Coordinate, and View
identities remain the exact original handles; value protection does not
deep-copy identity refs. This checkpoint does not extend that guarantee to
unenumerated live authoring values.

| Public owner | Detached values | Identity values retained exactly |
|---|---|---|
| `DirectSolveSpec`, `OperatorSpec`, and Direct quantity Specs | frequency grids, root hints, anchors, and evaluation frequencies | Coordinate handles |
| `PumpAxis`, `HBCaseSpec`, and `HBSolveSpec` | pump frequencies, drive currents, and the shared response grid | drive, Port, and Coordinate handles |
| `OptimizationVariable` and `CostObjective` | default/override bounds, target, weight, and optional scale | `ParameterRef`, selector, and bound View lineage |
| catalog-created `ComponentInstance` literal fields | validated literal physical quantities | existing `ParameterRef` bindings and component/Pin identity |
| `PortRef` | reference impedance | owning Plan and node identity |
| verified scalar, matrix, operator, HB, optimization, and sweep Results | decoded Quantities, arrays, mappings, and lazy point payloads when loaded | Result, point, parameter, and View identities |

Small declaration values are detached once. Large decoded Result arrays use
immutable backing and inexpensive read-only views, so reading a matrix does not
copy it and reading a lazy sweep does not load its point payloads.

## Physical fields bind refs to a Plan {#physical-parameter-binding}

Creating a definition does not assign it to a Plan. A Plan adopts a ref only
when both conditions hold:

1. a compatible physical factory field receives that ref; and
2. the resulting component is registered in the root Plan or one of its owned
   inline or reusable component scopes.

For example, `components.capacitor(..., capacitance=capacitance_ref)` creates
the physical consumer. Registering that capacitor in an owned subsystem makes
the binding part of the containing Plan. `ParameterSet` never registers a ref,
and there is no `CircuitPlan(parameters=...)` or scope-level target
`parameter(...)` declaration.

The Plan captures only the transitive closure of consumed definitions and
physical-field bindings. Adding an unused definition later cannot change its
snapshot. A ref may intentionally feed several fields or several Plans; every
Plan records only its own consumers. Equal-valued distinct refs remain
independent. A literal remains fixed and creates no ref automatically.

Plan-specific inspection, including fan-out, appears in the exact diagram
audit or an existing Plan/Run explanation bound to that Plan. Evidence names
the input identity, consuming component occurrence, physical field, baseline,
schema, and any accepted scalar `AffineMap`.

Unknown or unconsumed refs, incompatible schema or units, conflicting
definitions, unsupported physical fields, and bindings that become nonphysical
after mapping fail before execution. No ref is ignored or rebound by value.

## Reusable component boundary {#reusable-parameter-boundary}

A Library factory accepts compatible literals or `ParameterRef`s at its
declared inputs. Private physical fields consume them within the
`CompositePlan`. The factory may expose an already-bound ref:

```text
CompositePlan.expose_parameter(
    *, id: str, parameter: ParameterRef,
) -> ParameterRef
ComponentInstance.parameter(name: str) -> ParameterRef
```

For a primitive physical field bound directly to a `ParameterRef`,
`component.parameter(field_name)` returns that exact original object. This
includes scalar fields and transmission-line `length` and whole `rlgc` fields;
clone/add preserves the lookup and independent definition identity. A literal
field or unknown name raises `KeyError`, without creating an implicit ref.

A Composite instead requires explicit `expose_parameter()` for every public
lookup. Its lookup returns the exact original exposed ref; it does not derive
identity from the component path or expose a hidden child. Literal-only inputs
have no public ref to retrieve. For a primitive field bound through an
`AffineMap`, lookup returns the exact original input ref, retaining input units
and identity rather than the transformed physical value. Mapping and consumers
remain captured separately. Composite factory inputs are never automatically
published, whether directly bound or mapped.

One public ref may deliberately fan out to several fields. Existing
`AffineMap` support remains scalar-only and preserves its accepted support and
request-local extrapolation rules. Shared aliases of one ref cannot be treated
as independent optimization variables. Arbitrary Python callbacks,
expressions, and implicit interpolation are not parameter bindings.

## One immutable point {#parameter-set}

```text
ParameterSet(
    values: Mapping[ParameterRef, ParameterValue] | None = None,
    *, allow_extrapolation: tuple[ParameterRef, ...] = (),
) -> ParameterSet
```

A `ParameterSet` represents one point. At an operation boundary, omitted refs
consumed by the Plan use their captured baselines, producing one complete
effective ParameterSet. The caller's object and incoming mutable containers are
defensively copied and frozen.

A scalar ref accepts one compatible finite scalar Quantity, not an array.
Structured refs accept one compatible complete structured value. Unknown,
unconsumed, foreign, incompatible, non-finite, or multiply conflicting values
fail closed. Extrapolation authorization remains request-local and cannot be
inherited by a later request.

The effective point changes physical values, not authored pins, conductor
basis or order, reference conductor, section count, ownership, or topology.

## Ordered parameter spaces {#parameter-space}

```text
ParameterSpace.grid(
    *, axes: Mapping[ParameterRef, ParameterAxisValues],
    fixed: ParameterSet = ParameterSet(),
) -> ParameterSpace
ParameterSpace.points(
    points: Sequence[ParameterSet],
) -> ParameterSpace
```

`ParameterAxisValues` means a one-dimensional Quantity array or a finite
sequence of compatible scalar Quantities or complete `RLGC` values. The ref's
schema selects the scalar or structured form; one axis cannot mix them.

`grid()` forms a Cartesian product. Axes retain author order and iterate as
ordered nested axes: the first declared axis is outermost and the last declared
axis is fastest. Every axis is nonempty and one-dimensional. Scalar axes may use
Quantity arrays or sequences of compatible quantities. Structured axes use
sequences of complete compatible values. `fixed` and `axes` must be disjoint.

`points()` preserves the supplied ordinal order and duplicate positions. It is
not a Cartesian product. Both constructors freeze their inputs. Neither form
changes a Plan, creates a parameter definition, or attaches itself to one
Plan.

Each request that uses a space independently binds one Plan, the View or Views
selected by its calculation, and one calculation Spec, and revalidates that
Plan's consumption and definition compatibility. The same immutable space may
therefore be reused by another compatible Plan request. Full effective values
are captured at every point.
Frequency samples, Direct matrix channels, HB cases/modes, and Result array axes
remain calculation dimensions rather than parameter axes.

## Operations and exact resolution {#parameterized-operations}

The target extends the corresponding supported operations and exact resolution
with one keyword. `SolveSpec`, `EvaluationSpec`, and their single-point Result
unions are the existing operation-specific types in the Runtime Contract, not
new constructible classes:

```text
CircuitRun.solve(
    ref: NetworkViewRef, spec: SolveSpec,
    *, parameters: ParameterSet | ParameterSpace | None = None,
) -> SolveResult | ParameterSweepResult
CircuitRun.evaluate(
    ref: NetworkViewRef, spec: EvaluationSpec,
    *, parameters: ParameterSet | ParameterSpace | None = None,
) -> EvaluationResult | ParameterSweepResult
CircuitRun.resolve(
    ref: NetworkViewRef, spec: SolveSpec | EvaluationSpec,
    *, parameters: ParameterSet | ParameterSpace | None = None,
) -> SolveResult | EvaluationResult | ParameterSweepResult
CircuitRun.optimize(
    ref: NetworkViewRef, spec: OptimizationSpec,
    *, parameters: ParameterSet | None = None,
) -> OptimizationResult
CircuitRun.optimize(
    spec: OptimizationSpec,
    *, parameters: ParameterSet | None = None,
) -> OptimizationResult
```

`None` and `ParameterSet` return the operation's ordinary typed single-point
Result. Supplying a `ParameterSpace` always returns
`ParameterSweepResult`, including for a one-point space. The request identity
binds the exact Plan, View, Spec, operation, parameter-space form and order,
effective points, runtime, and dependency identities.

One sweep or optimization request executes its points in one Julia process.
SCNSim may reuse compatible topology/index preparation and type
specializations. It must rebind values and recompute every affected native
assembly, factorization, transform weight, and reduction at every point. It may
not reuse a nominal reduced matrix, create per-value generated types, or start
one Julia process per point.

`resolve(..., parameters=space)` reconstructs the same request and verifies the
stored batch. It never solves, retries, searches for a latest result, changes
point order, or substitutes another space. Lazy point access and chunked
artifacts avoid eager materialization without changing identity.

## Sweep Result and point outcomes {#parameter-sweep-result}

The public read-only surface is:

```text
ParameterSweepResult.points -> ParameterPointAccessor
ParameterSweepResult.plot(...) -> plotly.graph_objects.Figure
ParameterSweepResult.show(...) -> None
ParameterSweepResult.select(
    *, parameters: ParameterSet,
) -> ParameterSweepSelection
ParameterSweepResult.collect(
    *, quantity: QuantitySelector,
) -> ParameterField
ParameterSweepSelection.plot(...) -> plotly.graph_objects.Figure
ParameterSweepSelection.show(...) -> None
ParameterSweepSelection.collect(
    *, quantity: QuantitySelector,
) -> ParameterField
ParameterSweepSelection.points -> Sequence[ParameterPointOutcome]
ParameterField.plot(
    *, x: ParameterRef, y: ParameterRef | None = None,
) -> plotly.graph_objects.Figure
ParameterField.show(...) -> None
```

`ParameterPointAccessor` is a read-only lazy accessor with deterministic
iteration and length. Grid points support their Cartesian multi-index, such
as `points[2, 0]`; one integer is sufficient for a one-axis grid. Listed
points support their ordinal integer index. A selection's read-only lazy
sequence retains matching source-enumeration order.

Each immutable `ParameterPointOutcome` exposes:

- `parameters: ParameterSet`, the complete effective point;
- `source_index: int | tuple[int, ...]`;
- `succeeded: bool`;
- `result`, discriminated on success as the operation's existing
  `DirectSolveResult`, `HBBatchResult`, `DiagonalRootResult`,
  `DirectQuantityResult`, or `OperatorResult`; and
- `failure`, discriminated on numerical non-success as the preserved typed
  point failure.

Its derived `ParameterPointIdentity` binds exactly the batch
`ResultIdentity`, `source_index`, and `parameters_sha256`. The ordinary typed
point result carries this derived identity rather than claiming an independent
`ResultIdentity`. These accessor and identity types are not user-constructible
receipt or Result APIs; standalone operation Results retain their existing
`ResultIdentity`.

Reading success data from a failed point raises that preserved failure. It does
not return zero, NaN-as-success, a partial fake Result, or data from another
point. HB case outcomes remain nested inside the point's ordinary HB Result and
do not replace the outer point status. Every point Result remains a derived
view of the one batch receipt and exact point identity; it is not assigned a
fabricated independent attempt or receipt.

`select()` treats supplied entries as exact canonical-unit filters; omitted
refs are wildcards, not baseline defaults. It returns an immutable read-only
view of all exact matches. Its lazy ordered `points` preserve each outcome's
original source index, batch point identity, and duplicate position; selection
ordinals do not replace those identities. Empty matches produce an empty
selection and table, never a nearest or baseline fallback.

`collect()` accepts an existing typed `QuantitySelector`, never a string or
callback. Parent-sweep and selection collection use the same rule. A selector
absent from the request's Spec or Result family fails without execution. A
quantity that was requested but is missing at a numerically failed point
instead produces a masked entry linked to that preserved point failure. The
field retains units, original parameter-axis order and sample positions,
source indices, batch and point identities, and repeats.
Plot presentation keeps a failed sample as a non-numeric gap and displays its
source index, parameter identity, and typed reason. If every collected sample
failed, the default presentation is the complete status table rather than a
fabricated zero curve or a missing-data exception.

A complete Cartesian slice may be shown as a one-axis curve or labeled
two-axis grid after every other varying parameter axis has been fixed by exact
selection. Repeated parameter values remain distinct sample cells rather than
interpolation intervals. A listed, scattered, empty, or incomplete slice stays
an indexed point collection; it is not reshaped, averaged, or interpolated.
For `ParameterField.plot()`, leaving a non-displayed varying parameter axis
ambiguous, requesting this minimal plot surface for a non-scalar quantity, or
having no selected samples raises `ValueError`. Wrong argument types raise
`TypeError`. Frequency, channel, and HB axes cannot be implicitly dropped.
Native Plotly Figures are the numerical presentation surface; displaying them
never starts analysis.

An exact fixed-axis workflow is therefore:

```python
selected = sweep.select(
    parameters=ParameterSet({capacitance: 110.0 * u.fF})
)
selected.show()
line = selected.collect(quantity=root_spec.frequency)
line.show(x=inductance)
```

The selection keeps the original point identities; collecting from it neither
renumbers the points nor creates a receipt. Showing an empty collected
selection may report that no samples were selected; it cannot fabricate a
curve or numerical value.

## Failure boundary {#parameter-system-failures}

Wrong Python argument/container types raise `TypeError`. Well-typed but invalid
definitions, refs, units, schemas, shapes, consumption, Plan compatibility,
axis overlap, empty axes or point lists, duplicate axis identities, or
unsupported operation combinations raise the existing validation family before
execution.

Expected numerical non-success is retained at its exact sweep point while
other points may complete. If shared preparation encounters an expected
baseline-root numerical failure, that failure is retained at every dependent
sweep point; sharing the preparation does not reclassify it as a process or
protocol failure. Optimization retains its existing stricter boundary: failure
while evaluating its mandatory baseline fails the whole optimization request.
A malformed protocol, process failure, corrupt batch, receipt or artifact
mismatch, stale request, or integrity violation aborts or rejects the whole
request rather than fabricating per-point numerical failures. Nothing falls
back to a baseline, another Plan, an independent root, or a nearest stored
request.

## Optimization binding {#parameter-optimization-binding}

Every scalar `QuantitySelector` used by optimization is bound immutably to one
existing View with `selector.on(view)`. Binding is non-executing. It does not
evaluate the selector, create a View, or capture a Python callback.

A scalar optimization expression is an immutable closed tree. Its leaves are
`QuantitySelector` values; internal nodes are `QuantitySum`, subtraction with
`-`, and Python `abs(...)`. Constants, multiplication, division, and other
arithmetic are outside this surface. Operands must share one physical
dimensionality. Sums and differences use the leftmost operand's public unit
convention, including the existing hertz/radian-per-second conversion, and
absolute value preserves that unit. Tree order is semantic: repeated leaves
remain distinct ordered positions even when they share one underlying root.

Any expression may contain selector leaves bound to different Views; the View
belongs to each leaf rather than to the objective as a whole. Every leaf is
evaluated at the same candidate ParameterSet. Shared root dependencies are
reused without folding or deduplicating the expression positions.

`run.optimize(spec, ...)` requires every selector leaf to be explicitly bound.
The convenience form `run.optimize(default_view, spec, ...)` fills only
unbound leaves. Explicit leaf bindings always win. Both forms normalize to one
complete bound selector tree before canonical request encoding, and therefore
have the same request identity when their effective leaf bindings are equal.
The request envelope's primary View is derived from the first normalized leaf
in declaration order; it supports the existing Result lineage envelope but is
not the sole View of a multi-View optimization.

Every bound View must belong to the same `CircuitRun` and captured Plan.
Missing or foreign bindings and selector/View incompatibility fail before a
Julia process starts. One candidate is one complete effective ParameterSet
shared by all bound Views; it is not a collection of independently optimized
View-local points.

`OptimizationSpec.show()` is declaration-only: it presents the ordered
expression tree, each bound View, comparison, target, scale setting, weight,
bounds, and optimizer controls without a Run. `run.explain(...)` adds the
Run-dependent normalized binding, resolved scale, effective initial parameter
point, and runtime identity without creating an attempt.

`OptimizationVariable` continues to identify one scalar ref, finite physical
bounds, and its accepted transform. Bounds are not inferred from grid extrema,
the `ParameterSpec`, or the baseline. A parameter space is not an implicit set
of optimization requests.

Supported optimization accepts `parameters=ParameterSet(...)` for non-active
fixed refs. Active-variable and fixed-ref overlap is rejected; omitted
non-active consumed refs use the Plan baseline. Existing active initial value,
baseline root-continuation, objective, scaling, seed, population, candidate
failure, and extrapolation semantics remain owned by the Runtime Contract.

Every candidate and winner binds a complete effective ParameterSet. A caller
may explicitly pass the winner to a later calculation or parameterized diagram
without mutating the Plan baseline. No optimization score, plot, or diagram is
scientific acceptance or a Gate.

## Parameterized diagrams {#parameterized-diagrams}

```text
CircuitPlan.render_schematic(
    spec: CircuitDiagramSpec = CircuitDiagramSpec(),
    *, parameters: ParameterSet | None = None,
) -> CircuitDiagramResult
```

Rendering defaults to captured baselines and rejects `ParameterSpace`. The
same explicit point drives native values, compiled expansion, labels, expected
evidence, and independent observed A/B audit. The audit displays baseline
versus selected values, Plan-specific physical consumers, and
`parameters_sha256`, which identifies the complete effective point after
operation-time baseline filling rather than the caller's sparse override map.

Changing values does not mutate `plan_sha256`. It may change expanded,
omission, numerical, and presentation identities. For one exact Plan, complete
effective point, and representation, layout and Theme cannot change electrical
or structural facts. No promise is made that all digests are invariant across
points. Baseline-versus-selected labels are display provenance, not a
substitute for effective-point identity.

A diagram certifies only the supported authoring or compiled projection at
that point. It does not select or certify a View, solver Result, optimization,
or every request-local override. `show()` and existing read-only Schemdraw
Drawing/save and Notebook viewer surfaces serialize the same frozen audited
scene; they never execute analysis or patch stale evidence.

## Structured RLGC support boundary {#parameterized-rlgc-scope}

A complete compatible existing `RLGC` object is one structured parameter value.
Its R/L/G/C matrices preserve fixed conductor order, reference conductor,
shape, physical dimensions, source extraction, and provenance. Matrix rows and
columns are not separate sweep axes. `n_sections` remains authored structure.

The target supports one or several complete RLGC values for Direct/HB response
and applicable operator requests, subject to existing backend capabilities.
Every point performs its own full matrix stamps, both half-shunts, and required
value-dependent analysis. Scalar sweeps and baseline-root tracking at a fixed
Plan-baseline RLGC value remain supported.

This target does not support baseline-root continuation across changing RLGC
values, continuous whole-matrix optimization, or implicit interpolation.
Unsupported requests fail explicitly instead of replacing tracking with
independent root selection. This is the candidate's supported scope, not a
claim of mathematical impossibility.

## Identity and implementation alignment {#parameter-identity-alignment}

Canonical SI value encoding remains the physical identity mechanism. Target
parameter identity uses exactly definitions-collection ID plus local ID;
schema and canonical baseline remain immutable compatibility facts. Plan
snapshots add only consumed definitions and their physical-field bindings.
Batch identities preserve space kind, ordered axes or listed positions,
complete effective points, and duplicate ordinals.

The current runtime and V2 schema use definitions-collection ID plus local ID.
The shared scientific and protocol definitions live in
`identity-common.schema.json`; the V2 bundle owns current Plan, request, and
Result envelopes. Component-path parameter identities and old envelopes remain
historical evidence only, with no reachable compatibility schema or runtime
promised. Implementation integration does not accept this reopened scope.

## Performance and nonclaims {#parameter-system-nonclaims}

Lazy Cartesian enumeration and chunked storage avoid constructing one enormous
point list. Cold runtime preparation, Julia compilation, and per-point work are
different costs. This contract promises no timing threshold, JIT elimination,
daemon, distributed execution, or numerical-result cache across incompatible
points.

The Parameter System does not alter pins, topology, Views, physical models,
Direct/HB algorithms, objective definitions, Design Targets, scientific
interpretation, or Human acceptance. It creates no interpolation, tolerance
Gate, success threshold, or release claim.
